title: AI: enumerate legal actions
instructions:
Implement the legal-action enumerator in game-core/src/ai/enumerate.ts (NO classes, NO mutation, pure function). This is M2-T01: given a GameState and a seat, return EVERY action that is currently legal for that seat — the AI player's move menu, also used by the client UI. It GENERATES a bounded candidate set per action type and filters it through the engine's own validator, so it can never invent a move the apply-layer would reject.

Imports (exact, and ONLY these):
```ts
import type { Action, GameState, PlayerState, CardDef, CharacterAbility } from '../types';
import { validateAction } from '../engine/validate';
```
(The validator is the single source of truth. The enumerator's job is exhaustive-but-bounded candidate GENERATION; validateAction() decides legality. If both disagree, validateAction wins — that is the contract.)

STYLE RULES: strict TS with noUncheckedIndexedAccess — every array index read and every Map.get() must be guarded (`=== undefined` check) before use, with a sensible fallback (skip the candidate). No `any`. No default exports. Never mutate inputs. Export exactly ONE function:

```ts
export function enumerateLegalActions(state: GameState, seat: number): readonly Action[]
```

Behavior / algorithm (in this exact order; the returned array preserves this order — deterministic):

0. Guard: `const player = state.seats[seat];` — if undefined, return []. (PlayerState is not optional in the type but guard anyway per noUncheckedIndexedAccess.)

1. playActionCard: for every instanceId in player.hand (hand ORDER), look up its CardDef via state.cardDefs[state.cards[instanceId]?.cardId]. If the def exists and def.type === 'action', add `{ type: 'playActionCard', seat, instanceId }`. (validateAction will reject when actionsLeft is 0, wrong phase, etc. — that is fine and intended; we generate, it filters.)

2. playItem: same loop over player.hand for def.type === 'item' (hand order) -> `{ type: 'playItem', seat, instanceId }`.

3. playAmmo: same loop over player.hand for def.type === 'ammunition' (hand order) -> `{ type: 'playAmmo', seat, instanceId }`.

4. explore — generate weapon combinations from player.hand:
   a. Build `weaponsInHand` = instanceIds in player.hand whose def.type === 'weapon', in hand order.
   b. Ammo coverage helper (deterministic greedy): for a given list of weapons, compute totalAmmoReq = sum of def.ammoReq (0 if undefined). Take the ammo cards in player.hand whose def.type === 'ammunition', SORTED BY (bonuses.ammo DESC, then instanceId ASC — tiebreak for determinism), and greedily pick cards until the running sum of their bonuses.ammo >= totalAmmoReq OR no cards remain. The picked set (in hand order, NOT sorted order — keep hand order for the final action) is the ammoCards candidate. If totalAmmoReq is 0, ammoCards = [].
   c. Generate candidates: for EVERY single weapon in weaponsInHand (hand order) -> `{ type: 'explore', seat, weapons: [w], ammoCards: <greedy cover for [w]>, exploreCount: 1 }`. THEN for EVERY unordered PAIR (i < j) of weapons in hand order -> `{ type: 'explore', seat, weapons: [wi, wj], ammoCards: <greedy cover for the pair>, exploreCount: 1 }`. (Pairs enable Burst-Fire's plusDamagePerExtraWeapon and are the core multi-weapon tactic. v1 scope: singles + pairs only — documented in a comment. No triplets.)
   Note candance: a weapon with ammoReq > 0 but NO ammo in hand still yields a candidate — validateAction rejects it with 'explore: insufficient ammo' (empty ammoCards). Generating it is correct and harmless.

5. buy: for every pileId in state.marketPiles (Object.keys order = insertion order): add `{ type: 'buy', seat, pileId }`. (validateAction rejects unaffordable/empty piles.)

6. useCharacterAbility: look up the character def: `const charInst = state.cards[player.characterInstanceId]; const charDef = charInst ? state.cardDefs[charInst.cardId] : undefined;` If charDef?.abilities exists, for every index i in 0..abilities.length-1 add `{ type: 'useCharacterAbility', seat, abilityIndex: i }`.

7. endTurn: add `{ type: 'endTurn', seat }` — always (validateAction filters phase/turn).

8. chooseOption: for every prompt in state.prompts where prompt.seat === seat (prompts order), for every option index oi in 0..prompt.options.length-1, add `{ type: 'chooseOption', seat, promptId: prompt.id, option: oi }`.

9. Filter: `const results = [...generated].filter(a => validateAction(state, a).ok);` Return results. (validateAction is imported and called — never reimplemented.)

Determinism guarantee: same (state, seat) input ALWAYS returns the same array (same order, same contents). Tests rely on this.

----------------- File 2: game-core/src/ai/enumerate.test.ts -----------------

Vitest (globals). Copy this EXACT fixture, then write the tests:

```ts
import { enumerateLegalActions } from './enumerate';
import { validateAction } from '../engine/validate';
import type { Action, GameState, CardDef, PlayerState } from '../types';

function def(id: string, over: Partial<CardDef> = {}): CardDef {
  return { id, name: id, type: 'weapon', set: 'premier', text: '', copies: 1, ...over } as CardDef;
}

const DEFS: Record<string, CardDef> = {
  'ch-1': def('ch-1', { type: 'character', maxHp: 100, level2At: 4, abilities: [{ kind: 'generic', level: 1 }, { kind: 'generic', level: 2 }] }),
  'am-1': def('am-1', { type: 'ammunition', copies: 28, bonuses: { ammo: 10, gold: 10 } }),
  'am-2': def('am-2', { type: 'ammunition', copies: 28, bonuses: { ammo: 30, gold: 20 } }),
  'we-1': def('we-1', { type: 'weapon', cost: 20, ammoReq: 20, damage: 10 }),
  'we-2': def('we-2', { type: 'weapon', cost: 5, ammoReq: 0, damage: 8 }),
  'we-3': def('we-3', { type: 'weapon', cost: 0, ammoReq: 10, damage: 15, weaponEffects: [{ kind: 'plusDamagePerExtraWeapon', amount: 5 }] }),
  'ac-1': def('ac-1', { type: 'action', cost: 20, bonuses: { gold: 10 } }),
  'it-1': def('it-1', { type: 'item', itemEffects: [{ kind: 'healFixed20OrTrashWithSecondFor60' }] }),
  'ma-1': def('ma-1', { type: 'infected', hp: 20, attack: 10, decorations: 1 }),
};

function player(seat: number, over: Partial<PlayerState> = {}): PlayerState {
  return {
    seat, name: 'P' + seat, controller: 'human',
    characterInstanceId: 'ch-1#' + seat, hp: 100, maxHp: 100,
    decorations: 0, level: 1 as const,
    turnAmmo: 0, turnGold: 50, actionsLeft: 1, buysLeft: 1, exploresLeft: 1,
    weaponDamageBonusThisTurn: 0, attached: [],
    inventory: ['inv1', 'inv2', 'inv3', 'inv4', 'inv5', 'inv6', 'inv7', 'inv8'],
    hand: [], discard: [], playArea: [], downed: false, dead: false,
    ...over,
  };
}

function baseState(over: Partial<GameState> = {}): GameState {
  const s: GameState = {
    version: 1, seed: 1, rngState: 1, phase: 'main', activeSeat: 0, turnNumber: 1,
    seats: [player(0), player(1)],
    marketPiles: {
      hg: { pileId: 'hg', cards: ['we-1#1'] },
      kn: { pileId: 'kn', cards: ['we-2#1'] },
    },
    mansionDeck: ['ma-1#1', 'ma-1#2'], mansionBottom: [], removed: [],
    cards: Object.fromEntries(['ch-1#0', 'ch-1#1', 'am-1#1', 'we-1#1', 'we-2#1', 'we-3#1', 'ac-1#1', 'it-1#1', 'ma-1#1', 'ma-1#2'].map(id => [id, { instanceId: id, cardId: id.replace(/#.*$/, ''), location: { zone: 'hand' as const, index: 0 } }])),
    cardDefs: DEFS,
    prompts: [], winners: [], endReason: undefined, log: [],
    ...over,
  };
  return s;
}

const act = (a: Action): Action => a;
```

Tests (exactly these; assert via the returned array):

1. 'no legal actions for an unknown seat' — enumerateLegalActions(baseState(), 99) deep-equals [].
2. 'every returned action passes the validator' — s = baseState() with seats[0] having hand ['am-1#1', 'we-1#1', 'ac-1#1', 'it-1#1'] (in that order); for every action in enumerateLegalActions(s, 0): validateAction(s, action).ok === true (loop with expect).
3. 'hand cards produce one action per playable card' — s = baseState({ seats: [player(0, { hand: ['am-1#1', 'am-1#1', 'ac-1#1', 'it-1#1'] }), player(1)] }); acts = enumerateLegalActions(s, 0); count act.type === 'playAmmo' == 2; 'playActionCard' == 1; 'playItem' == 1; and there is exactly one playAmmo action with instanceId 'am-1#1' (dedupe not required — duplicates are legal since two ammo cards are distinct instances; keep both).
4. 'buy candidates for every market pile' — s = baseState(); acts = enumerateLegalActions(s, 0); the buy actions' pileIds sorted == ['hg', 'kn'] (both affordable: gold 50 >= 20 and >= 5).
5. 'explore singles and pairs with greedy ammo' — s = baseState({ seats: [player(0, { hand: ['we-1#1', 'we-2#1', 'we-3#1', 'am-1#1'] }), player(1)] }); acts = enumerateLegalActions(s, 0); explores = acts.filter(a => a.type === 'explore' && a.seat === 0) as Array<Extract<Action, { type: 'explore' }>>; expects: length 6 (3 singles + 3 pairs); one single with weapons ['we-2#1'] and ammoCards [] (ammoReq 0); one single with weapons ['we-1#1'] and ammoCards ['am-1#1'] (greedy cover: 10 ammo >= 20? NO — am-1 gives 10, totalAmmoReq 20 -> insufficient; greedy picks am-1#1 anyway, validator REJECTS that single explore) — so instead assert: the explore with weapons ['we-2#1'] has ammoCards []; there is exactly ONE explore with weapons ['we-1#1'] in the FILTERED result only if the ammo covers it — in this fixture it does NOT (only 10 ammo < 20), so the filtered list has NO we-1 single explore. Assert: filtered explores' weapons arrays == exactly [['we-2#1'], ['we-3#1']] singles (we-3 needs 10 ammo -> am-1#1 covers exactly) plus the 3 legal pairs: we-2+we-3 (ammoReq 10 covered), we-1+we-2 (20 covered), we-1+we-3 (30 -> am-1#1 gives 10, NOT covered -> rejected). So filtered explore set (compare as sets of JSON strings of the weapons+ammoCards projection): [ ['we-2#1'], ['we-3#1'], ['we-2#1','we-3#1'], ['we-1#1','we-2#1'] ] — i.e. 4 explores total in the final result. Assert by mapping filtered explores to JSON.stringify({ w: a.weapons, a: a.ammoCards }) and expecting the set of those 4 exact strings (via expect.arrayContaining + length 4, or Sort). IMPORTANT: document this reasoning in a comment in the test. If the greedy tiebreak makes a different but validator-legal ammo choice for we-3's pair, prefer the assertion that ALL returned explores validate AND the we-2-bare and we-2+we-3 and we-1+we-2 forms are present — the count of 4 and the exact ammoSets as computed above are the spec's expected values; trust the greedy rule (sort bonuses.ammo desc, am-1#1 is the only ammo card so any tiebreak collapses to it).
6. 'ability actions for each character ability index' — s = baseState(); acts = enumerateLegalActions(s, 0); filter type 'useCharacterAbility'; map to abilityIndex sorted == [0, 1] (ch-1 has 2 generic abilities).
7. 'endTurn always generated and legal when active' — s = baseState(); acts = enumerateLegalActions(s, 0); contains exactly one endTurn action; and the WAITING seat gets an empty list: enumerateLegalActions(s, 1) deep-equals [] (not your turn for play/buy/endTurn; player(1) hand is empty; no prompts).
8. 'prompts produce one chooseOption per option' — s = baseState({ prompts: [{ id: 'p1', seat: 0, text: 'choose', options: ['a', 'b', 'c'] }, { id: 'p2', seat: 1, text: 'other', options: ['x'] }] }); acts = enumerateLegalActions(s, 0); chooseOption actions: 3 with promptId 'p1' (options 0,1,2), NONE with promptId 'p2'; the p1 options set == [0,1,2].
9. 'deterministic: same input same output' — s = baseState({ seats: [player(0, { hand: ['am-1#1', 'we-1#1', 'we-2#1', 'ac-1#1'] }), player(1)] }); expect(enumerateLegalActions(s, 0)).toEqual(enumerateLegalActions(s, 0)); also JSON round equal via toEqual on the arrays directly.
10. 'no explores when hand has no weapons' — s = baseState({ seats: [player(0, { hand: ['am-1#1', 'ac-1#1'] }), player(1)] }); acts = enumerateLegalActions(s, 0); no action has type 'explore'.
11. 'dead player still gets endTurn for cleanup' — s = baseState({ seats: [player(0, { dead: true }), player(1)] }); acts = enumerateLegalActions(s, 0); every returned action validates ok; expected EXACTLY [{ type: 'endTurn', seat: 0 }] (play/buy/explore/ability all rejected for dead players; endTurn is allowed).

Do NOT add or reorder tests; do not add exports. If a computed detail differs from the spec's expected values, the TEST file is what gates — make the implementation match the algo above exactly, because the values in tests 5/11 were derived from it.
